title: Central infinitesimal multiplicative extensions of tori and their character sequence
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], fix an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $E,T$ be affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $T$ be a torus and let $q:E\to T$ be a finite faithfully flat homomorphism, meaning that $k[E]$ is a finite faithfully flat $k[T]$-module via $q^*$. Assume that $N=\ker q$ is infinitesimal, central in $E$, and of multiplicative type. Infinitesimal means that $k[N]$ is local with nilpotent augmentation ideal, and central means that $N(A)$ commutes with $E(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Tori and multiplicative type are as in [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type]. Then $E$ is commutative and of multiplicative type. For a separable closure $k^s/k$ [def-pd-separable-closure], write $X^*(D)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k^s\text{-grp}}(D_{k^s},\mathbf G_{m,k^s})$ for a group $D$ of multiplicative type, with its natural continuous Galois action [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality]. Pullback and restriction give an exact sequence of finitely generated abelian groups with Galois action $$0\longrightarrow X^*(T)\xrightarrow{q^*}X^*(E)\longrightarrow X^*(N)\longrightarrow0,$$ where $X^*(T)$ is free of finite rank and $X^*(N)$ is finite. No smoothness or reducedness assumption on $E$ or $N$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 12.22, printed p.239, and Theorem 12.23, p.240. Agent synthesis: for a central infinitesimal kernel the commutator descends to the reduced scheme T x T and is trivial, then apply commutative multiplicative extension and exact character antiduality. This is a supporting lemma for Proposition 17.80(b), p.378, rather than the torus-lifting conclusion itself.

proof.text: Put $F=\bar k$. Coordinate rings of base changes and kernels are tensor pushouts by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-sc-group-scheme] and [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Thus $q_F$ remains faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], and its kernel is $N_F$. The augmentation ideal of $F[N_F]=F\otimes_k k[N]$ is $F\otimes_k I$, where $I=\ker(\epsilon:k[N]\to k)$; if $I^a=0$, its extended ideal also has $a$th power zero and the quotient is $F$. Centrality remains true because every $F$-algebra is a $k$-algebra. By [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], $T_F$ is split and $N_F$ embeds in a split torus; [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable] makes $N_F$ diagonalizable. For the next two steps work over $F$, suppressing subscripts. The map $p=q\times q:E\times E\to T\times T$ is faithfully flat: it factors into two base changes of $q$. Faithful flatness of the factors follows from the base-change node, and that of their composite follows because the composite scalar-extension functor is exact and detects zero modules, as in [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Corollary 12.22 and Theorem 12.23, printed pp.239–240; agent-supplied commutator descent and explicit character-kernel calculation.

proof.text: The morphism $c:E\times E\to E$, $(x,y)\mapsto xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$, has $q(c(x,y))=1$, since $T$ is commutative, so factors through $N=\ker q$ by [def-sc-group-scheme]. On the overlap $(E\times E)\times_{T\times T}(E\times E)$, its two pullbacks agree: for every algebra $A$, two lifts satisfy $x'=xn$, $y'=ym$ with $n,m\in N(A)$, and centrality gives $(xn)(ym)(xn)^{-1}(ym)^{-1}=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$. These are equalities of morphisms, since they hold on points over every algebra (in particular the coordinate algebra of the overlap). Write $R=F[T\times T]$ and $B=F[E\times E]$. By [lem-pc-cech-exact] with module $R$, $R\to B$ is the equalizer of $b\mapsto b\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. Consequently every $c^*(a)$, $a\in F[N]$, lies in $R\subset B$. The unique preimage assignment $a\mapsto\bar c^*(a)$ is an $F$-algebra map, because the inclusion $R\to B$ is injective. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] it defines $\bar c:T\times T\to N$ with $c=\bar c\circ p$.

source.place: Tag 023M, lemma-ff-exact, applied in degree zero; explicit central commutator calculation supplied by Q41. This realizes the commutator-descent sentence of the item source.

proof.text: The coordinate algebra $R$ of the split torus $T\times T$ is reduced: write it as $F[\mathbf Z^{2r}]$ and apply the field-extension/domain clause of [lem-trf-split-lattice-torus-projection] with base field $F$ and extension $F/F$. The identification with the coordinate torus, including its group law, is the first clause of [lem-trf-lattice-torus-coordinates-action]. Every element of the augmentation ideal $J$ of $F[N]$ is nilpotent by step 1, so its image under $\bar c^*:F[N]\to R$ is zero. Since $F[N]/J=F$, this map is exactly the identity-point map followed by constants. Hence $c=1$, and $E_F$ is commutative. This also proves commutativity over $k$: the two coordinate maps for multiplication and opposite multiplication become equal after tensoring with $F$, and the map $k[E\times E]\to k[E\times E]\otimes_k F$ is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-field-extension-base-change-faithfully-flat] and [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective].

source.place: Corollary 12.22 and Theorem 12.23, printed pp.239–240; agent-supplied commutator descent and explicit character-kernel calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-commutative-multiplicative-type-extension] over the algebraically closed field $F$ to $N_F\to E_F\to T_F$. The coordinate map is faithfully flat by step 1; both ends are diagonalizable (for $T_F$, its split-torus presentation is $D_F(\mathbf Z^r)$); and the middle group is commutative by step 3. It follows that $E_F$ is diagonalizable, hence embeds into a split torus: choose finitely many generators of its character group $M$, and use the surjective Hopf map $F[\mathbf Z^s]\to F[M]$. The affine closed-immersion criterion [def-weil-closed-immersion] turns this into a closed embedding. Thus $E$ is of multiplicative type by [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type].

source.place: Corollary 12.22 and Theorem 12.23, printed pp.239–240; agent-supplied commutator descent and explicit character-kernel calculation.

proof.text: Now work over $K=k^s$. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], the groups $E_K,T_K,N_K$ have split presentations $D_K(M),D_K(L),D_K(P)$ with $M=X^*(E)$, $L=X^*(T)$, $P=X^*(N)$ finitely generated and carrying their stated continuous Galois actions. Naturality identifies $q^*$ with a homomorphism $u:L\to M$ and the coordinate map with $e_l\mapsto e_{u(l)}$: a character labelled $l$ pulls back to the one labelled $u(l)$. The coordinate map is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-base-change], hence injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with module $K[L]$. If $u(l)=0$, the element $e_l-e_0$ maps to zero, so basis independence gives $l=0$. Thus $u$ is injective.

source.place: Corollary 12.22 and Theorem 12.23, printed pp.239–240; agent-supplied commutator descent and explicit character-kernel calculation.

proof.text: The kernel fibre product in [def-sc-group-scheme], with the algebra tensor pushout of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], has coordinate algebra $K[M]\otimes_{K[L]}K=K[M]/(e_{u(l)}-1\mid l\in L)$. Put $C=M/u(L)$. This quotient is $K[C]$: the forward map sends $e_m$ to $e_{[m]}$, and the inverse sends $e_{[m]}$ to the class of $e_m$. It is well-defined since $m'=m+u(l)$ gives $e_{m'}=e_me_{u(l)}=e_m$ in the quotient. Both maps preserve the Hopf operations on these basis elements and are inverse. Thus $N_K\simeq D_K(C)$, with the inclusion into $E_K$ induced by $M\to C$. By the natural character identification in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], restriction $M\to P$ is this quotient map followed by an isomorphism $C\simeq P$. It is surjective with kernel $u(L)$. Together with step 5 this proves the displayed short exact sequence. Both maps commute with Galois action: conjugating a character and then composing with the $k$-defined $q$ or inclusion is the same as composing first and then conjugating.

source.place: Corollary 12.22 and Theorem 12.23, printed pp.239–240; agent-supplied commutator descent and explicit character-kernel calculation.

proof.text: Over $F$, the split presentation of $T_F=\mathbf G_m^r$ gives its character group $\mathbf Z^r$: its coordinate Hopf algebra is $F[\mathbf Z^r]$, and [lem-sfb-group-algebra-group-like-basis] says that the images of $t$ under Hopf maps $F[t,t^{-1}]\to F[\mathbf Z^r]$ are exactly the $e_l$. The scalar-extension compatibility in [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality] identifies this group with $L=X^*(T)$. Hence $L$ is free of finite rank. Finally $N$ has finite-dimensional coordinate algebra: a finite set of $k[T]$-module generators for $k[E]$ maps to a spanning set of $k[E]\otimes_{k[T]}k=k[N]$. Extending to $K$ keeps this spanning set finite, whereas $K[N_K]=K[P]$ has basis $e_p$ indexed by $P$. Basis independence forces $P$ to be finite. None of these arguments assumes that $E$ or $N$ is reduced or smooth.
